skill.name: typography
skill.description: Guidance for selecting distinctive fonts, pairing typefaces, and using strong scale and weight contrast.
skill.summary: Design sharper typography with distinctive fonts, contrast, and scale.
skill.author: Crossbill-Highlights

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive. The referenced line gives typography quality guidance and does not request system inspection, secret access, network activity, or command execution.

static_findings.snippet: Typography instantly signals quality. Avoid using boring, generic fonts.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 5 says typography signals quality and advises against generic fonts. This is design guidance, not system reconnaissance or any request to inspect the host environment.

content.value_statement: Generic font choices can make polished work feel unfinished. This skill guides stronger font selection, pairing, contrast, and scale for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Recommends distinctive font families for code, editorial, technical, and expressive design contexts.
Discourages common default font choices when stronger visual identity is needed.
Guides high contrast type pairing, such as display with monospace or serif with geometric sans.
Suggests stronger weight and size jumps for clearer visual hierarchy.
Encourages decisive use of one distinctive font loaded from Google Fonts.
limitations: It does not include CSS snippets, design tokens, or implementation files.
It does not verify font licensing, performance, or language coverage.
It does not provide accessibility testing for readability or contrast.
It gives compact guidance, not a full brand typography system.

use_cases.title: Improve Product Interface Type
use_cases.description: Choose stronger fonts and hierarchy for dashboards, tools, and application screens.

use_cases.title: Refine Marketing Page Typography
use_cases.description: Create more memorable headlines and supporting text with better font pairing and scale.

use_cases.title: Guide AI Design Reviews
use_cases.description: Ask an assistant to critique font choices and recommend more distinctive alternatives.

prompt_templates.title: Pick Better Fonts
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner typography selection for a new page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this interface concept and suggest a stronger typography direction. Avoid generic default fonts and explain the font role for headings and body text.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Font Pairing
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate font pairing for a product or content page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create three font pairings for this project. Use high contrast between roles and include one option from Google Fonts.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Visual Hierarchy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of scale, weight, and contrast.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this typography hierarchy. Recommend stronger size jumps, weight choices, and pairing changes while keeping the layout professional.

prompt_templates.title: Define a Typography Direction
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced system guidance for a brand or application.
prompt_templates.prompt: Define a concise typography direction for this product. Include font family choices, usage roles, weight ranges, scale guidance, and tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: A technical documentation site uses a plain system font for every text role.
output_examples.output: Use IBM Plex Sans for body text and IBM Plex Mono for code labels. Increase heading weight and size for clearer hierarchy.

output_examples.input: A landing page needs a more editorial and premium type direction.
output_examples.output: Pair Playfair Display for headlines with Source Sans 3 for supporting copy. Use a large headline scale and restrained body weights.

output_examples.input: A developer tool interface feels polished but visually forgettable.
output_examples.output: Use Space Grotesk for headings and JetBrains Mono for technical details. Keep one distinctive voice and avoid mixing too many families.

best_practices: Choose one distinctive primary font and apply it consistently.
Use strong contrast between type roles for clear hierarchy.
Check readability, language support, and load performance before shipping.
anti_patterns: Using generic default fonts when the project needs a clear visual identity.
Combining too many typefaces without defined roles.
Relying on small weight or size changes that users barely notice.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps choose distinctive fonts, pair typefaces, and create stronger hierarchy through scale and weight.

faq.question: Does it write production CSS?
faq.answer: No. It provides design guidance and font direction, not implementation code.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it require external tools?
faq.answer: No. It mentions Google Fonts as a source, but it does not run network requests or install anything.

faq.question: Is this useful for brand work?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide early typography direction for brand, product, and content experiences.

faq.question: What should I verify before publishing?
faq.answer: Check font licensing, accessibility, language coverage, and page performance in your final implementation.
